pr_title: Highlight all search results while the search box is open
pr_body:
Hi!  First time contributor,  wanted to try to add highlighting for all search results.

## Summary of the Pull Request
Update to highlight all search results

## References and Relevant Issues
Closes #7561

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments
Follows the existing selection code as much as possible.
Updated logic that finds selection rectangles to also identify search rectangles.
Added structure to ShapedRow to track the search selections.

## Validation Steps Performed

## PR Checklist
- [ ] Closes #xxx
- [ ] Tests added/passed
- [ ] Documentation updated
   - If checked, please file a pull request on [our docs repo](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/terminal) and link it here: #xxx
- [ ] Schema updated (if necessary)

@lhecker just a quick heads up, I think this is ready for another round of reviews.  (No rush just wasn't sure what the protocol for alerting you was).

Honestly, after reading through it once, I couldn't find any other obvious flaws. If you don't mind, I'll wait a bit before I approve it though, because I want to think about it some more.

Long-term I want to simplify the rendering code, so that you don't need to implement a bunch of methods to introduce a feature like this one. I'd like to make it so that there's a "rendering payload" struct, similar to the `RenderingPayload` for `AtlasEngine` which simply describes what should be rendered and it's up to the rendering implementation to do with that information whatever it wants. So, for instance, instead of you calling into AtlasEngine to say "render these highlights now", you'd just fill the highlight vector on the `RenderingPayload` and then whenever AtlasEngine wants to it pulls out the relevant data. That way we skip an entire layer of code. The same would apply to cursors, selections, text colors, fonts, etc., etc.
I'm basically trying to see how I can make this PR fit with that. I won't ask you to modify your PR though. I'm just trying to map out what I need to do. 🙂

While writing my previous comment I realized that Chromium changes the background and foreground color of text when marking it as highlighted: 
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/assets/2256941/9b4080bc-3229-4758-ae97-8563e94e00c3)

It also doesn't seem to care about the current background color because picking the same color makes the highlight invisible:
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/assets/2256941/b6fc51b6-d6f0-4fc7-bc8f-a5a7829531f3)

Should we perhaps do the same? Get rid of `_drawSearchSelections` and just manipulate the background/foreground colors of the highlighted text (see second half of `AtlasEngine::PaintBufferLine`)?

Residential selection expert, @DHowett, what say thee? `#5fff0000`, aka `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.37)` overlay or fixed `#ff9632` background with `#000000` foreground color, like Chromium?

issue_context.title: Feature Request: Highlight all finding
issue_context.body:
# Description of the new feature/enhancement

A good and handy feature  will be the option to highlight all the find when using the ctrl+shift+f 
Something like the GitBash alt+f3 search option:

![2020-09-08_16-01-42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6774998/92480374-7a52a080-f1ed-11ea-8850-f1988c2019c1.png)


This is really helpful when looking for something or doing some comparison
comments: I actually like how the terminal scrolls to the next selection when searching a term but this can be useful too. Can this be an optional sub-setting?
Please to implement this - it's dreadfully useful 🙏

review_comments:
I was expecting to find something here poking the renderer.. like `TriggerSelection`. Is that already happening because we're also making a new selection when we search?

I am worried about the hidden coupling here.

I think right now it is relying on this call to trigger selection.  https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/9b823b03e47e9fbcaf321761123cf22f0ee7bcdd/src/cascadia/TerminalControl/ControlCore.cpp#L1624

Something does feel weird when I compare it to have the normal selection from _search.SelectCurrent() works.

Would it make sense to move the _searcher.HighlightSelections() here?  https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/9b823b03e47e9fbcaf321761123cf22f0ee7bcdd/src/cascadia/TerminalControl/ControlCore.cpp#L1622

Or to add a TriggerSelection call here?  https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/9b823b03e47e9fbcaf321761123cf22f0ee7bcdd/src/cascadia/TerminalControl/ControlCore.cpp#L1608

That's a really good question. I think that you'll want to do it any time you are done changing `_searchSelections`. @lhecker might have a better opinion here.

I tried out your branch! It works really, really well. Congrats!

I only found one issue.

When I delete the search with backspace, or close it, the highlights stick around... but the search is no longer active. So next time the screen updates, they all go away.

I think this might be because of the missing `TriggerSelection`!

somewhat long story on the selections not getting cleared when the last char is deleted from the search box.  I was trying to match the behavior from the release that I had on my machine and it looked like the "current" selection highlight stuck around after deleting the last char and then I cross referenced visual studio and it looked like it also left the highlights so I thought it might be a pattern and didn't want to change any existing behavior.

For clearing all selections, I think this would work.
https://github.com/e82eric/terminal/commit/4dc6305455d06c3cf6d05da08ccec2d6f32151ed

For leaving the current selection highlighted but clearing all of the other highlights, I think this would work.
https://github.com/e82eric/terminal/commit/3854b8bc78fca4a00ee0159738197ec0004b5656

For clearing the selections after the search box is closed,  I actually like the behavior where it leaves the selections highlighted,  It gives me context if I want to go into mark mode (about what is going to get selected).

I think it is possible to clear the selections after closing the search box.
https://github.com/e82eric/terminal/commit/8a613530d512f9f9c1bef5bf27c23d7eed06df7c

Let me know if any of these make sense or if there is another approach and I can update the PR.
@lhecker do we need to use any of your locks here?

I'd say no. I moved all locking calls to outside of the `Terminal` class to make the code more consistent. If you were talking about the `_assertLocked()`, then I'd also say no, because this will be indirectly covered through the `_VisibleStartIndex` (we could add `_assertLocked()` to all member functions in the future if we wanted to).

Conhost performance question: it's cheap to return an empty vector, right?

Gut check... it looks like it is "cheap enough", at least on x64:

```c++
#include <vector>
std::vector<int> foo() {
    return {};
}
```
```nasm
__$ReturnUdt$ = 32
std::vector<int,std::allocator<int> > foo(void) PROC  ; foo, COMDAT
$LN13:
        sub     rsp, 24
        xor     eax, eax
        mov     QWORD PTR [rcx], rax
        mov     QWORD PTR [rcx+8], rax
        mov     QWORD PTR [rcx+16], rax
        mov     rax, rcx
        add     rsp, 24
        ret     0
std::vector<int,std::allocator<int> > foo(void) ENDP  ; foo
```
